# Remaining-mutant review

Every supplied .rs file in upstream-tests-1.99.0 was searched by content, including excluded std tests and helpers. The snapshot contains seven files, not the whole Rust repository. Matching statements and their surrounding code were inspected. Broad regex matches, source lines, context and hashes are retained in [survivor-review.json](evidence/gen/survivor-review.json). All 109 source doc blocks were also reviewed, including excluded examples. No assertion for a surviving witness was found in this supplied material. The separate whole-tree review below extends the content search; neither review proves universal test absence.

Whole-tree search (review, 2026-10-09): the 1.99.0 coretests and benches, library/std net unit tests and TCP/UDP tests, core doc tests outside net, tests/ui, Miri, Clippy and rustfmt tests were searched by content. No covering assertion for any of the 19 named witnesses was found. Std net unit tests and Miri were checked by reading; they were not run under the mutants. Other Rust versions and online history were not searched. No network search was performed.

The 19 cases comprise 12 behavioural cases (7 distinct behaviours; six whitespace cases are one rule) and 7 optional representation snapshots. The FromStr impls are heavily tested in coretests `parser.rs:25–110` and `ip_addr.rs:9–120`; the missing cases name only specific behaviours. No remaining mutant is equivalent. Each has a concrete stable public-API assertion that passes on the restored copy and real std 1.99.0, then fails at runtime after its source edit. The failure observes a changed value, output string or parse result. Compiler failures are not accepted as witnesses. The assertion and runtime difference are recorded individually below and in the JSON receipt. M095 changes an observable formatting policy; ambiguity of a recommendation does not make the mutation equivalent. No equivalent mutant needed removal.

## M073: SocketAddrV6 FromStr: parses the maximum numeric scope id

Search pattern: `4294967295|u32::MAX|scope_id|SCOPE_ID`.

Maximum scope values are constructed and formatted in the core and std socket tests. Parsing uses scope 1337. No maximum-scope parse assertion occurs in the supplied files. The whole-tree review also found coretests `benches/net/addr_parser.rs:93` parsing `[fe80::1%4294967295]:443` in a benchmark without an assertion.

Observable witness:

```rust
// generated by Codex gpt-6.1-sol on 2026-10-07 for Ivo Matijasevic
assert_eq!("[::1%4294967295]:0".parse::<SocketAddrV6>().unwrap().scope_id(),u32::MAX);
```

[Baseline green](evidence/gen/M073-baseline.txt), [runtime difference](evidence/gen/M073-proposed.txt), [real std green](evidence/gen/proposed-real-std.txt).
